AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'Land stop-work-order gate (issue #980, UMR-a63f) - PR 274' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  resource_governor.py                               | 279 +++++++++++++++
 tests/test_dispatch_owner_task_status_write.py     |   5 +
 tests/test_dispatch_owner_task_tmux_relay_lock.py  |   5 +
 tests/test_ocid_artifact_links.py                  |   8 +
 tests/test_ocid_evidence_supersession.py           |   4 +
 tests/test_rule3_no_premature_umr_minting.py       |   4 +
 tests/test_rule6_zero_duplication_by_ocid.py       |  10 +
 ...st_run_tick_continues_past_row_resolved_skip.py |   5 +
 tests/test_stop_work_order_gate.py                 | 397 +++++++++++++++++++++
 9 files changed, 717 insertions(+)
Evidence Recorded: The gate's structure (submit()-time check plus dispatch_one() defense-in-depth, tuple-of-order-ids, task_kind scoping limited to the only PR/push-capable kind, extensive tests) is sound, but its core security primitive does not deliver the guarantee its own docstring claims: _git_committed_file_text() reads `git show HEAD:<path>` in whatever branch happens to be checked out in the shared, live AI_OS working directory at call time -- it never verifies that HEAD is on the trunk branch (e.g. main) or has been pushed to/merged on origin. The docstring for this function explicitly asserts the fix works because a fabricated exemption 'once pushed, is caught by whatever review this repo already requires for that branch,' but the code enforces no such thing -- a purely local `git commit` (or simply `git checkout` onto a branch with a favorable commit already sitting on it) on the exact same laptop/server filesystem satisfies the check just as well as a reviewed, merged PR would, with zero GitHub involvement. This is not hypothetical: checking the live AI_OS repo right now (the same VERIDIAN_AI_OS_DIR/OWNER_DECISIONS_PATH default this code reads in production) shows it currently checked out on a non-main branch (docs/hard-rule3-correction-...) whose HEAD commit message is 'Owner: lift stop-work order (issue #980), decided directly on server' -- i.e. the exact ambient-HEAD instability this gate's whole design depends on not existing is the live, present state of the very file it reads. Given this PR's explicitly stated threat model is a 'compromised or fabricating' dispatched worker, and such a worker has the same filesystem/git access to AI_OS as anything else running there, this gap lets that same actor defeat the gate through a trivially easier route (local commit, no push, no PR, no review) than the one the code was written to close. Secondary, lower-severity: the 'stop-work-order-lifted' branch returns None (lifting the gate entirely) as soon as ANY approved entry contains that substring in its id, without checking which specific order in STOP_WORK_ORDER_TASK_IDS it corresponds to -- fine while only one order is ever open, but the tuple is explicitly documented to grow, and an entry meant to lift one order would silently lift all of them. Recommend a follow-up that pins the read to the actual trunk branch and/or verifies the commit is reachable from (or matches) origin/<trunk> before treating it as authoritative, plus scoping the lifted-check to a specific order id. Issues found: _git_committed_file_text()/_owner_decisions_committed_entries() trust whatever branch is checked out at git HEAD in the live, shared AI_OS directory -- not origin/main or any pushed/reviewed ref -- so a local, unpushed commit (by any actor with shell access to the same box, including the 'compromised or fabricating' worker this PR's own docstring names as the threat) is sufficient to fabricate an approved exemption or a full stop-work-order-lifted record, defeating the gate without ever touching GitHub review. Confirmed live: /opt/veridian/ai-os is currently checked out on a non-main branch whose HEAD commit message reads 'Owner: lift stop-work order (issue #980), decided directly on server.'; 'stop-work-order-lifted' entries lift the gate for ALL orders in STOP_WORK_ORDER_TASK_IDS at once, with no check against which specific order id the entry is lifting -- fine today (single order) but will silently over-lift once a second concurrent order is appended, as the module's own comments say to expect.; Not a workflow-file change; no .github/workflows/** touched, hard rule not implicated.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.

AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'sweep-adopt-veridian-scripts-276-land-stop-work-order-gate-issue-980-umr' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  resource_governor.py                               | 279 +++++++++++++++
 tests/test_dispatch_owner_task_status_write.py     |   5 +

 tests/test_stop_work_order_gate.py                 | 397 +++++++++++++++++++++
 9 files changed, 717 insertions(+)
Evidence Recorded: The mechanism itself (a deterministic STOP_WORK_ORDER_TASK_IDS gate checked against git-committed HEAD content of OWNER_DECISIONS_PATH, wired into both submit() and dispatch_one() as defense-in-depth, with 9 new test cases covering block/allow/exemption-scope/uncommitted-edit-rejection paths) is a reasonable, fail-closed design and correctly reuses the existing RULE2_OUTCOME_MAP wiring, but independent verification against the live /opt/veridian/ai-os git history directly contradicts a core claim baked into the shipped code comments: the gate's own docstring asserts 'given none exists as of this gate's own creation, every order named above is open,' yet a real, git-committed, status:approved 'stop-work-order-lifted-2026-08-08-v2' entry (commit 2a46f43, 'Owner: lift stop-work order (issue #980)') has existed in OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_2026-07-23.yaml since 2026-08-08, more than a week before this diff was authored -- a directly falsifiable claim that is false, matching this codebase's recurring pattern of confident-but-unverified incident narratives in dispatched task work. That false claim, combined with this diff adding a new fail-closed git-subprocess dependency to the core submit()/dispatch_one() path (any git failure or repo-state change silently blocks ALL future veridian_task_create dispatch system-wide, referencing a now-resolved incident) and a scope-fidelity gap where the 'lifted' check ignores the real lift entry's stated file-scope and unblocks unconditionally, means this is not the low-blast-radius additive change tier1 assumes; it should not merge as-is. Issues found: Code comments/docstrings in resource_governor.py (_stop_work_order_block_reason) assert no committed stop-work-order-lifted entry exists 'as of this gate's own creation' -- false. A real, git-committed, status:approved 'stop-work-order-lifted-2026-08-08-v2' entry has existed in /opt/veridian/ai-os/OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_2026-07-23.yaml since commit 2a46f43 (2026-08-08T11:01:14Z, 'Owner: lift stop-work order (issue #980)'), over a week before this diff. This is a directly falsifiable, verified-false claim baked into shipped code, and it casts doubt on the rest of the elaborate incident narrative (UMR-20260807-110133-205d, task-20260807-150203, PRs #269/#250/#251, 'nine dispatches that declined') used to justify the gate, none of which could be independently corroborated in this review.; submit() and dispatch_one() now shell out to git on every veridian_task_create call to read OWNER_DECISIONS_PATH at HEAD; any git failure, permission issue, detached HEAD, or relocation of the ai-os repo causes the check to fail closed and block ALL future task creation system-wide (referencing an already-resolved 2026-08-06 incident) -- a new, silent, system-wide failure mode added to core dispatch logic, inconsistent with an 'additive/low-blast-radius' tier1 change.; The 'stop-work-order-lifted' id match in _stop_work_order_block_reason ignores the real lift entry's own stated scope ('for all PR/push work on resource_governor.py, superboss-register.py, task-gateway.py, and resource_governor_tick_loop.sh') and instead unconditionally unblocks ALL veridian_task_create submissions once any approved '*-lifted*' entry is found -- looser than what was actually Owner-approved (currently harmless since it happens to be over- rather than under-permissive today, but it is not implementing the real approved scope).; STOP_WORK_ORDER_TASK_IDS' hardcoded default bakes a single already-resolved historical task id into shared production code as a standing 'presumed open' order; its currently-inert behavior depends entirely on the ai-os git history retaining the 2026-08-08 lift commit and OWNER_DECISIONS_PATH keeping its current default -- a latent trap that could silently start blocking all task creation if that history or default ever changes.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
